articles.title: CMBS Conduit Capital Focuses Heavily on Multifamily, Office Sectors
articles.narrative: The latest conduit CMBS data from CRED iQ indicates a lending market that has become more selective rather than more cautious, with multifamily and office sectors emerging as exceptions to the trend of increased equity requirements for borrowers. Multifamily loans saw an increase in loan-to-value (LTV) to 62% and a significant drop in rates to 6%, signaling strong lender confidence. Office loans also experienced higher LTVs at 49.5%, but with thinner debt service coverage ratios, suggesting lenders are underwriting more aggressively based on perceived cash flow stabilization rather than a full return of confidence. Other property types, including retail, self-storage, and industrial, faced stricter lending terms with lower LTVs and higher debt yields, requiring more sponsor equity despite easing rates.

articles.title: Commercial Real Estate Investment’s Curious Rise Amid Higher Inflation, Rates
articles.narrative: Despite persistent inflation and rising interest rates, commercial real estate investment activity has shown surprising resilience, with significant increases in investment sales volume in the first half of 2026. This counterintuitive trend suggests that the industry is adapting to a new economic reality where instability has become the norm. One expert posits that the relevance of minor interest rate adjustments has diminished for sophisticated investors, who are instead prioritizing asset value, potential for appreciation, and exit strategies. The abundance of global capital, including a "mountain of available capital" in private equity, is also driving continued investment as funds seek deployment opportunities beyond traditional low-yield options.

articles.title: New York State’s Opportunity Zones Deadline Is Fast Approaching
articles.narrative: New York State is preparing to announce its updated Opportunity Zone (OZ) designations by September 28, following the permanent renewal and revision of the federal program. State and city officials, including Gov. Kathy Hochul and Mayor Zohran Mamdani, have already implemented policy changes to accelerate affordable housing development, but the revised OZ program is expected to attract additional investment into underserved communities. The new federal guidelines aim to direct capital more effectively to distressed areas by adjusting poverty level requirements and offering greater tax incentives for rural investments, which has reduced the number of eligible tracts nationwide. Developers are keenly awaiting the state's selections, particularly for areas where projects are already in the pipeline, to ensure continuity for investors.

articles.title: Affinius Capital, Alliance Residential Dispose of 545-Unit Seniors Housing Portfolio in Northern California
articles.narrative: A joint venture between Affinius Capital and Alliance Residential has sold a two-property seniors housing portfolio in Northern California. The portfolio, comprising 545 units across Sonrisa Senior Living in Roseville and The Watermark at Almaden in San Jose, was acquired by a publicly traded REIT. This transaction represents one of the largest seniors housing portfolio sales in the region in recent years.

articles.title: Newmark Brokers Sale of Four-Building Industrial Portfolio in Silicon Valley

articles.title: Livmark, Hillside to Develop 185-Unit Multifamily Community in Longmont, Colorado

Greystar has been tapped to manage the property upon its anticipated completion in fall 2027.

articles.title: Walbridge launches Chicago-based data center firm
articles.narrative: Walbridge, a Detroit-based construction firm, has launched L5 Mission Critical, a new Chicago-headquartered company specializing in comprehensive data center services. The new entity will offer services from commissioning and site readiness to critical operations, retrofits, and project management. This strategic move aims to address the rapidly expanding data center market, driven by AI and cloud growth, and provide integrated solutions for both third-party clients and Walbridge's construction projects.

articles.narrative: Marcus & Millichap has brokered the sale of a net-leased Walgreens property in Austintown, Ohio, for $3.25 million. The buyer was a private local investor. The property has been operating as a Walgreens for over two decades and is situated in a prominent retail corridor.

data_points.notable_features: Located within a retail corridor alongside several national retailers.
data_points.project_notes: Property has operated as a Walgreens for more than 23 years.

articles.title: BOMA study: Commercial real estate remains a boon to the U.S. economy
articles.narrative: A new study by the Building Owners and Managers Association International (BOMA) highlights the significant economic impact of commercial real estate across the U.S. The report, which covers 35.4 billion square feet of commercial property in 79 markets, found that the operation and maintenance of office, retail, and industrial assets generate $609.9 billion in annual economic output and support 3.9 million jobs. The study also notes that for every dollar spent on building operations, $2.22 in total economic output is generated, underscoring the broad network of businesses and workers supported by the sector. Additionally, the research points to the growing influence of data centers on office construction statistics and sustained high levels of industrial construction.

articles.title: Colliers negotiates sale of 31,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Stafford

The property, situated on 1.89 acres, features a versatile layout including office, assembly, fulfillment, shop, and showroom areas. Both the seller and the buyer were represented by Colliers brokers in the transaction.

articles.title: RIVANI Lands $114.3M Refi on Miami Beach Office/Retail Project
articles.narrative: RIVANI has secured a $114.3 million refinancing package for its recently completed office and retail development in Miami Beach. The financing, provided by BridgeInvest, will be used to retire existing debt on the 165,170-square-foot property, which is currently 83% leased. The project underwent a significant $38 million renovation after RIVANI acquired it in 2024 for $62.5 million.

data_points.notable_features: The property features a full-service concierge and valet, spa, fitness and wellness center, meditation room, podcast studio, and a Tokyo-inspired speakeasy.
data_points.project_notes: RIVANI acquired the property for $62.5 million in 2024 and subsequently launched a $38 million renovation. The firm is seeking voter approval for an estimated $50 million expansion above the parking garage, adding approximately 47,000 square feet.

articles.title: USF Breaks Ground on $500M Mixed-Use Venture
articles.narrative: The University of South Florida (USF) and its development partners have broken ground on the initial $500 million phase of Uptown Landing, a new mixed-use project in Tampa. This first phase, spanning 30 acres, will feature student housing, graduate student and employee apartments, retail space, a hotel and conference center, and academic research facilities. The project is being delivered through a master development agreement with ACE Fletcher, a partnership formed by Capstone Development Partners, Aureate Development, and Ellison Development, with completion anticipated in fall 2028.

data_points.notable_features: Located within walking distance of the planned USF on-campus football stadium.
data_points.project_notes: Funding includes $270 million in tax-exempt bond financing and a $225 million investment for the Translational Research Institute.

articles.title: Mold Is Growing Into Major Problem For Apartment Owners
articles.narrative: The presence of mold is escalating into a significant concern for apartment owners, as evidenced by recent multimillion-dollar verdicts in mold-related lawsuits. This trend highlights the increasing financial and legal risks associated with mold issues in residential properties.

articles.title: Office Owners Pulling Back On Flexible Leases As AI Clouds Future Of Work
articles.narrative: Manhattan office landlords are reportedly reducing the flexibility offered in lease agreements. This shift comes amidst growing uncertainty regarding future office space requirements, largely driven by the potential impacts of artificial intelligence on work patterns and corporate real estate strategies.
